description: This image presents a series of five unquantified bar charts illustrating different relative distribution patterns. The horizontal axis serves as the category axis, displaying five distinct pattern labels below their respective charts: "Increasing", "Uniform", "Decreasing", "Spindle", and "Bottleneck", arranged sequentially from left to right. There is no vertical value axis, scale, value range, units, or tick marks provided; the heights of the bars represent relative, unquantified values. Each of the five labeled patterns consists of a group of four adjacent bars colored light green with black outlines. In the "Increasing" chart, the bar heights strictly increase from left to right, with the shortest bar on the far left and the tallest on the far right. The "Uniform" chart features four bars of identical height. The "Decreasing" chart displays bars that strictly decrease in height from left to right, starting with the tallest bar and ending with the shortest. The "Spindle" chart consists of short first and fourth bars of equal height, flanking two taller middle bars of equal height. Conversely, the "Bottleneck" chart features tall first and fourth bars of equal height, with two shorter middle bars of equal height between them. The bars are not stacked, and there is no specific visual emphasis, such as shading or bolding, applied to any individual bar or group.
